title: BalancerPoolerV2.migrateMint unbounded per-unit mintFor loop scales O(amount) and can become un-callable for large id-4 holders
severity_rationale: Low. Availability / UX failure for whales with concentrated id-4 holdings, not theft. The function is all-or-nothing per call: a holder with >~500 id-4 NFTs in a single wallet cannot complete migration in one tx without exceeding mainnet block gas (~30M). The revert is safe (id-4 is un-burned) and the holder has an on-chain workaround (split via safeBatchTransferFrom across multiple wallets) — operationally feasible for a retail user, friction for a custodian. Econ-scanner explicitly rejected this as Medium because the on-chain side has no value-leak path. Per C4: QA/Low (function-incorrect-as-to-spec for the stated 'all holders can migrate' framing). Fix is cheap (mintForBatch) and would also resolve part of DEDUP-L01.
description:
migrateMint accepts `uint256 amount` and executes `for (uint256 i; i < amount; ++i) { INFTMinterV2(minter).mintFor(NEW_NFT_INDEX, mintRecipient); }`. Each iteration is a full external call into NFTMinterV2.mintFor which validates authorizedMinters[msg.sender], validates configs[index].dispatcher != address(0), executes OZ ERC1155 _mint (one balance SSTORE, one supply SSTORE, one TransferSingle event, and the receiver-acceptance-check call) and emits ClaimMintedFor. Realistic per-iteration cost: ~35k-60k gas depending on recipient code and existing balance slots. The test suite documents the stated worst case as N=41 (test_migrateMint_multiNFTLoop_41), so the project has implicitly assumed cohorts will be tens of NFTs, not hundreds.

If the original id-4 distribution concentrated NFTs on a treasury, market maker, or single power user (>~500 id-4 NFTs in one wallet), that holder cannot complete migration in a single transaction on mainnet without exceeding the ~30M block gas limit. There is no `migrateMintPartial(uint256 amount, ...)` and `amount` must equal the holder's intended migrate count — chunking has to be managed at the calling-tx level.

This duplicates the same scaling pattern flagged in report-6 RAW-005 (NFTMigrator.migrate) for the V1->V2 case. The fix is identical: add `mintForBatch(index, recipient, quantity)` to NFTMinterV2 that calls `_mint(recipient, index, quantity, '')` once, and have migrateMint call it once.
exploit_path:
1. Alice (or a treasury / market maker that accumulated id-4 NFTs during the original BalancerPoolerV2 lifetime) holds 800 id-4 NFTs.
2. Alice calls migrateMint(800, alice). burn succeeds (one cheap ERC1155 _burn with quantity=800). The loop begins.
3. At ~40k gas per mintFor, the loop alone budgets to ~32M gas — over the mainnet block gas limit.
4. The transaction reverts. Alice's 800 id-4 NFTs are un-burned (revert rolls back). She has not lost NFTs but cannot migrate via this entry point.
5. On-chain workaround: split id-4 across N fresh wallets via safeBatchTransferFrom and call migrateMint from each. For a custodian / institutional holder this may be operationally infeasible (compliance / signing-policy constraints).
mainnet_realism_check: Mainnet block gas limit is ~30M. ERC1155 _mint cost is well documented. The test suite explicitly stops at N=41, indicating the team has not stress-tested against large concentrations.
recommendation:
Replace the per-unit loop with a single batched mint. Add `mintForBatch(uint256 index, address recipient, uint256 quantity)` to NFTMinterV2 (gated by authorizedMinters[msg.sender]) that calls `_mint(recipient, index, quantity, '')`, then rewrite migrateMint to:
  `INFTMinterV2(minter).burn(msg.sender, OLD_NFT_ID, amount);`
  `INFTMinterV2(minter).mintForBatch(NEW_NFT_INDEX, mintRecipient, amount);`
This converts O(amount) external calls to O(1). Also collapses the partial-state window in DEDUP-L01.
